definitions.explanation: the state of having no hair on the head, or a bald spot
a patch of ground or surface with no vegetation or covering

examples.japanese: {父|ちち}は{若|わか}いころから{禿|はげ}を{気|き}にしていた。
examples.english: My father has been self-conscious about his baldness since he was young.

examples.japanese: {最近|さいきん}{頭頂部|とうちょうぶ}に{禿|はげ}ができてきたので、{育毛剤|いくもうざい}を{使|つか}い{始|はじ}めた。
examples.english: Since a bald spot has started forming on the top of my head recently, I started using hair growth tonic.

examples.japanese: {山|やま}に{禿|はげ}ができている。
examples.english: There is a bare spot on the mountain.

examples.japanese: {芝生|しばふ}の{禿|はげ}た{部分|ぶぶん}に{種|たね}をまいた。
examples.english: I sowed seeds on the bare patch of the lawn.

examples.japanese: {森林|しんりん}{伐採|ばっさい}で{山腹|さんぷく}に{大|おお}きな{禿|はげ}ができ、{土砂崩|どしゃくず}れの{危険|きけん}が{高|たか}まった。
examples.english: Deforestation created large bare patches on the mountainside, increasing the risk of landslides.

notes:
Can refer to both human baldness and bare patches on landscapes. When used about people, this word is considered direct and can be rude or insulting — handle with care in conversation. The verb form {禿|は}げる means "to go bald" or "to become bare."

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {禿|はげ}{頭|あたま}: bald head
- {禿|はげ}ができる: a bald/bare spot forms
- {丸|まる}{禿|はげ}: completely bald
- {禿|はげ}{山|やま}: treeless mountain

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {薄毛|うすげ}: thinning hair — a more polite and indirect way to refer to hair loss
- {脱毛|だつもう}: hair loss — medical or clinical term
- {禿|は}げる: to go bald/become bare — the verb form
